title: Air India Partners With Ministry of Tourism to Boost Incredible India Globally
excerpt: The MoU will leverage Air India's five-continent network and the government's Incredible India initiative to drive co-branded marketing, transit tourism, and trade engagement.
body:
• Air India and India's Ministry of Tourism have signed an MoU to jointly promote India as a premier global tourism destination through co-branded campaigns.
  • The partnership will extend Incredible India branding across Air India's 40 international destinations, digital platforms, and inflight experiences.
  • Collaboration includes transit tourism development at Delhi and Mumbai hubs, plus engagement with State Tourism Boards and trade partners.
  • Air India's 25 codeshare and 120+ interline partnerships connect India to over 1,000 destinations, amplifying the campaign's global reach.

Air India and India's Ministry of Tourism have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to jointly position the country as a top-tier global tourism destination. The agreement ties Air India's expanding international network — spanning 40 destinations across five continents — to the government's flagship Incredible India campaign, creating what both sides describe as a natural pairing of aviation reach and nation branding.

The MoU establishes a framework for coordinated work across tourism marketing, destination storytelling, trade engagement, transit tourism, and visitor experience enhancement. Under the agreement, both organizations will collaborate on co-branded global marketing campaigns across digital, social media, inflight branding, and other consumer-facing platforms, according to a report in MediaBrief.

Scope of the Partnership

The collaboration goes well beyond advertising. Air India and the Ministry will jointly engage with tour operators, travel trade partners, and industry stakeholders across key international markets. Activities will include participation in tourism exhibitions, roadshows, familiarisation trips, and other market development efforts designed to increase interest in India among international travellers.

"As the airline that proudly carries India in its name, Air India has a unique responsibility to showcase the country to the world and serve as an ambassador for the 'new India' that is confident, vibrant, warm, and welcoming."

— Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer, Air India

Air India's new-generation aircraft, digital platforms, and inflight experiences will serve as channels for bringing the Incredible India narrative directly to travellers. The partnership also envisions extending Incredible India branding across Air India's broader touchpoints, from airport lounges to booking platforms.

The airline and Ministry will also work with State Tourism Boards to highlight destinations across the country and support tourism-led regional initiatives.

Transit Tourism and Loyalty Tie-Ups

A notable element of the MoU is its focus on transit tourism. As Air India continues to develop Delhi and Mumbai into major international gateway hubs, the agreement provides for collaboration on stopover programmes that encourage transit passengers to spend time exploring India rather than simply passing through.

Both organizations will also explore aligning Air India's Maharaja Club loyalty programme with tourism experiences, developing customer incentives linked to cultural attractions, heritage sites, museums, and other visitor offerings. The Ministry of Tourism will facilitate engagement with stakeholders to create special offers and benefits for Air India passengers.

"This MoU reflects months of close collaboration between Air India and the Ministry of Tourism and a shared belief that aviation and tourism can be powerful partners in advancing India's global profile."

— P. Balaji, Group Head – Governance, Risk, Compliance & Corporate Affairs, Air India

Air India's Global Footprint

The partnership capitalizes on Air India's significantly expanded network. The airline currently serves destinations across North America, the UK and Europe, Australia, Africa, and Asia — regions home to nearly 95% of the world's population. Beyond its direct routes, Air India's 25 codeshare partnerships and more than 120 interline agreements connect India to over 1,000 destinations worldwide.

This reach has grown through a series of recent partnership moves. In June 2026, Air India signed an MoU with Thai Airways for a codeshare partnership spanning multiple continents. The airline has also struck interline deals with carriers including airBaltic, Bulgaria Air, Cyprus Airways, and Uzbekistan Airways, extending its footprint into the Baltics, Eastern Europe, the Mediterranean, and Central Asia.

Part of a Broader Tourism Push

The Air India agreement fits into a wider pattern of the Ministry of Tourism forging strategic partnerships to promote India internationally. Recent months have seen the Ministry sign MoUs with Google India for digital tourism promotion and with Mastercard for payment solutions and experiential tourism. Earlier, Tourism Australia signed a three-year marketing agreement with Air India to boost Indian visitor arrivals.

For India's diaspora, the partnership carries practical implications. Improved transit tourism programmes at Delhi and Mumbai could make stopover visits more attractive for NRIs transiting through India, while co-branded marketing campaigns may spotlight lesser-known destinations that diaspora travellers might explore on trips home. The integration of tourism incentives with Air India's loyalty programme could also reward frequent diaspora flyers with cultural and heritage experiences across the country.

The MoU's full scope of initiatives will be rolled out progressively, though neither side has disclosed specific campaign launch dates or financial commitments attached to the agreement.
